goals.0: Buying a ticket: einfach / hin und zurück
grammar.0.title: Official time (trains, TV, offices)
grammar.0.note: Train times are on the 24-hour clock: „vierzehn Uhr fünfunddreißig“. In everyday speech: „halb drei“ and so on.
grammar.1.title: Useful questions at the station
grammar.1.note: Verbindung = not just “connection”; it also means a route option on a train journey.
grammar.1.rows.0.1: When does the next train to … leave?
grammar.1.rows.1.1: Which platform does it leave from?
grammar.1.rows.3.1: Do I have to change trains?
grammar.2.text: Der Zug fährt um 14:35 Uhr ab. / Der Zug kommt um 18:10 Uhr an. / Ich steige in Nürnberg um. — The prefix (ab, an, um) goes to the end of the sentence. With a modal verb: „Ich muss in Nürnberg umsteigen“ (the whole verb goes to the end).
quiz.7.why: The modal verb is in second place, the whole verb goes at the end.
quiz.8.prompt: What is the article of Gleis?
quiz.9.prompt: Put the sentence in order: “When does the next train leave?”
quiz.9.why: A W-question: the verb is in second place.
